solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Thing for drink (3,2,3)

blocks.note: thing in the sense of a liking, as in 'it's not really my thing'
a hot drink, the British staple, served in the vessel the first word names

annotation.walkthrough: 'Thing' is used in the sense of a liking, as in 'it's not my thing' = 'not my cup of tea'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that is your cup of tea is your thing, the kind of thing you enjoy.

entries.clue: It ruined large deck on lawn (6,9)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A garden deck so big that it wrecked the lawn it was built on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun for the deck, but it is the definition: 'it' is an old euphemism for sex.
annotation.definitionFit: Carnal knowledge is sexual intercourse, which 'it' coyly stands for, as in 'doing it'.

entries.clue: City father lawyer shows round uni (5)

indicatorNotes.round: the lawyer goes round the university

blocks.note: pa = father
DA = district attorney, an American lawyer
U = university; it goes inside D…A

annotation.surface: A dad who is a lawyer giving someone a tour of a university campus.
annotation.walkthrough: Padua is an Italian city with one of Europe's oldest universities, which suits the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Padua is a city in north-east Italy.

entries.clue: Skill City fail to crack (8)

indicatorNotes.crack: to crack something is to break it open, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Manchester City's failing to crack a defence, as a football report might put it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a football club, but it is just four letters mixed with FAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: Facility is skill or ease in doing something, as in a facility for languages.

entries.clue: Be one stone under limits for eco-tax (5)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, I and ST sit below EX
indicatorNotes.limits for: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of ECO-TAX
I = one, the Roman numeral
ST = stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

annotation.surface: A demand to keep one's weight below the thresholds of some environmental levy.
annotation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the philosophical sense: 'to be or not to be' asks whether to go on existing.

entries.clue: Rouse support to expel a Republican (4,2)

indicatorNotes.to expel: one letter is thrown out of the support

blocks.note: a stirrup supports a rider's foot
R = Republican; one R is expelled from STIRRUP

annotation.surface: A political call to arms: stir up the base and throw out a Republican.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as American politics, but 'support' is a piece of riding tack.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to provoke people into feeling or action.

entries.clue: Where a cineaste might go matters (6)

blocks.note: split into two words: a direction word, then 'pics', slang for the cinema
matters in the sense of subjects under discussion

annotation.surface: Where a film buff chooses to go is a matter of importance.
annotation.walkthrough: The pics are the pictures, the cinema; the first half is a cryptic reading of the answer split into two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the plain one of subjects on an agenda, and the whimsical split into a trip to the pictures.

entries.clue: Adolescents primarily into phone calls … sound familiar? (4,1,4)

indicatorNotes.primarily: only the first letter of Adolescents is used
indicatorNotes.into: the letter goes into the calls

blocks.note: a ring and a bell are both informal words for phone calls
first letter of ADOLESCENTS; it goes inside RING…BELL

annotation.surface: Teenagers glued to their phones, a picture most parents will find familiar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give me a ring' and 'give me a bell' both mean phone me; a bell is British slang for a call.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that rings a bell sounds familiar, stirring a memory.

entries.clue: Real genius keeps working out for fun (8-7)

annotation.definitionNote: 'for fun' is a phrase describing a motive; the answer is an adjective for someone driven by it

indicatorNotes.working out: the letters are worked out, solved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A true genius keeps going to the gym just for enjoyment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a container instruction, but its letters are all part of the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, descriptive definition: the answer describes a motive, and 'for fun' names that same motive.

entries.clue: Brobdingnagian moorhen or mouse-sized bears (8)

indicatorNotes.bears: the phrase bears, carries, the answer inside it

blocks.note: hidden in moorhEN OR MOUSe-sized

annotation.surface: Giant bears that are only the size of a moorhen or a mouse, which is absurd.
annotation.walkthrough: Brobdingnag is the land of giants in Gulliver's Travels. The joke is that giant bears are said to be tiny.
annotation.definitionFit: Brobdingnagian means gigantic, after Swift's land of giants.

entries.clue: USSR operation for content censorship (9)

blocks.note: the Soviet Union was Red, communist
an action is a military operation

annotation.surface: A Soviet campaign to censor what the papers could print.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair picture of Soviet censorship, which hides that USSR is just RED.
annotation.definitionFit: Redaction is blacking out parts of a document's content before release.

entries.clue: Coppers pressure crook to give up leader (5)

indicatorNotes.to give up leader: the crook loses its first letter

blocks.note: P = pressure, the physics symbol
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods; minus its leader F it gives ENCE

annotation.surface: Police officers leaning on a criminal to make him give up his boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police but means copper coins, British pence.
annotation.definitionFit: British pennies are copper-coloured coins, so pence are coppers.

entries.clue: One into retro-rock and Help! (5)

indicatorNotes.into: into means entering the inside of something, so the I is placed inside the reversed rock
indicatorNotes.retro: retro means backwards, so the rock is turned round

blocks.note: lava is molten rock; turned round it becomes AVAL
I = one; it goes inside AVA…L

annotation.surface: A fan getting into retro rock and the Beatles album Help!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retro-rock' reads as a music genre, but 'retro' reverses the rock.
annotation.definitionFit: Avail is help or benefit, as in 'to no avail'.

entries.clue: Film performers screen: Renegades (9)

indicatorNotes.screen: the performers screen, surround, the film

blocks.note: turns are acts on a variety bill
a film is a thin coat or layer; it goes inside TURN…S

annotation.surface: A film poster: performers on screen in a movie titled Renegades.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' and 'screen' both suggest cinema; film is a coating and screen is a verb, to surround.
annotation.definitionFit: Turncoats are people who desert their side, renegades.

entries.clue: Design a bespoke NT monitor (4,4,2)

indicatorNotes.Design: the letters are designed into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A request to design a custom-made computer display for the National Theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: NT reads as the National Theatre, and 'monitor' as a screen; both are misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for close watching, the tabs being records or accounts kept on someone.

entries.clue: Imagine worker possessing a big belly? (9)

blocks.note: 'I imagine so' = 'I expect so'
the worker ant

annotation.surface: Picture a labourer with a large beer belly.
annotation.walkthrough: The big belly looks like a beer gut; the question mark flags that it is a pregnant belly.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: the answer is used of a mother awaiting a baby, whose bump shows.

entries.clue: Voice disapproval at royals’ reservations (8)

blocks.note: to boo is to voice disapproval
kings are royals

annotation.surface: Protesters jeering at the royal family's reluctance, their reservations about something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reservations' looks like doubts but means hotel or restaurant bookings.
annotation.definitionFit: Bookings are reservations of seats, rooms or tables.

entries.clue: Effects of drugs (4)

blocks.note: effects = belongings, one's kit
British slang for illegal drugs

annotation.surface: The effects that drugs have on a user.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Effects' reads as consequences, but it is personal effects, belongings.
annotation.definitionFit: Gear is both one's kit or belongings and a slang word for illegal drugs.

entries.clue: Praiseworthy God a nonsense, I’m told (8)

indicatorNotes.I’m told: what I am told is what I hear, so the answer sounds like the words clued

blocks.note: God = the Lord; nonsense = bull

annotation.surface: Someone reporting the claim that praising God is nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone works in non-rhotic British speech, where LORD and LAUD sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Laudable means deserving praise.

entries.clue: I’m sorry brief cuddle repelled (4)

indicatorNotes.brief: brief means cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.repelled: pushed back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: to spoon is to cuddle, lying curled together; cut short it is SPOO, then turned round

annotation.surface: An apology for a quick hug that was pushed away.
annotation.walkthrough: Spooning is lying curled together; 'repelled' fits the rejected hug but means reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Oops is what you say when you make a slip, a quick apology.

entries.clue: Police propose and second tailing criminals (10)

indicatorNotes.tailing: to tail is to follow, so TABLES comes after CONS

blocks.note: cons = convicts
to table a motion is to propose it
S = second

annotation.surface: A motion in a committee that the police should tail criminals, duly proposed and seconded.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage to table a motion is to put it forward. 'Second' also looks like seconding the motion, but it is just S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural noun for the lowest rank of British police officer, so the police as a body.

entries.clue: A small seabird near back of ship (6)

blocks.note: A as printed
S = small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

annotation.surface: A little seabird perched near the stern of a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The seabird flying about the stern is a real picture, and it hides that A and small are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A nautical term: the stern is the rear of a vessel, and anything at or behind it lies there.

entries.clue: Key authority presiding over problematic Yale opening (9)

annotation.definition: Key authority presiding over problematic Yale opening

blocks.note: reads like an important official, but it is an expert on keys
reads like the head of Yale University at a troubled inaugural event, but it is someone working on a stuck Yale lock

annotation.surface: A leading official presides over a troubled opening ceremony at Yale University.
annotation.walkthrough: Yale is a well-known brand of door lock as well as a university.
annotation.definitionFit: A locksmith is the expert on keys who is called when a Yale lock will not open.

entries.clue: Artist beginning to prefer husband to female (5)

indicatorNotes.to prefer: to prefer one thing to another is to choose it instead, so H replaces F
indicatorNotes.to: marks the letter that is dropped in favour of H

blocks.note: first = beginning, as in 'at first'
H = husband; it takes the place of F
F = female, the letter swapped out

annotation.surface: An artist starting out who would rather have a husband than a woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Damien Hirst is the British artist famous for a shark in formaldehyde.
annotation.definitionFit: Damien Hirst is a leading British artist.

entries.clue: Note lead falling from house — duck! (5)

indicatorNotes.lead falling from: the house loses its first letter

blocks.note: do is the first note of the sol-fa scale
a lodge is a house; minus its lead L it gives ODGE

annotation.surface: A warning shout as a piece of lead roofing falls off a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal, falling from a roof; it is the leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To duck is to dodge, avoid something by moving quickly.

entries.clue: City hotel I managed to turn around before (5)

indicatorNotes.to turn around: the word for managed is turned round
indicatorNotes.before: the reversed word comes before hotel and I

blocks.note: led = managed, was in charge; turned round it becomes DEL
H = hotel in the NATO alphabet
I as printed

annotation.surface: A traveller in a city hotel who managed to turn things around.
annotation.walkthrough: The blocks are listed in the order the answer reads; the clue gives hotel and I first and puts reversed LED before them.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: India's capital region is one city among many.

entries.clue: Tool stuck on end of merry-go-round — duck! (5)

indicatorNotes.end of: only the last letter of merry-go-round is used
indicatorNotes.stuck on: the tool is stuck on after that letter

blocks.note: last letter of MERRY-GO-ROUND
a rake is a garden tool

annotation.surface: A tool caught on a fairground ride, with a warning to duck as it swings round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck!' looks like a warning, echoing 24 across, but here it is the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the word names the male of the species, and 'duck' covers both sexes.

entries.clue: Big air lad pulled takes the biscuit (9)

indicatorNotes.pulled: the letters are pulled about, distorted

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A lad who pulled off a big air jump on his board: that really takes the biscuit.
annotation.walkthrough: A garibaldi is a British biscuit with a layer of squashed currants. 'Takes the biscuit' is an idiom for being outrageous, here taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: The garibaldi is a well-known British biscuit.

entries.clue: Worrying defeat with British sent packing (6)

indicatorNotes.sent packing: sent away, so the letter for British is removed

blocks.note: a beating is a defeat
B = British; it is sent packing from BEATING

annotation.surface: A worrying loss in which the British team were knocked out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worrying' is an adjective in the surface, but it means bothering, as in 'what's eating you?'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiomatic sense: a problem that gnaws at your mind troubles you, as in 'what's bugging you?'.

entries.clue: Police leader catches out-of-head Lord driving (8)

indicatorNotes.catches: the police leader catches, holds, the lord inside
indicatorNotes.out-of-head: the lord loses his head, his first letter

blocks.note: Sting was the lead singer of the band The Police
a lord is a peer; without its head P it gives EER, inside ST…ING

annotation.surface: A police chief arresting a drunk-driving lord.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Police leader' looks like a chief constable, but it is Sting, frontman of The Police. 'Out-of-head' suggests drunk and means beheaded.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean guiding a vehicle's course, as at the wheel.
